info.text: Interactive check questions for Lesson 13.2: The TEI Processing Model, ODD Customization, and Presentation Styles.

name.text: 01 Question: From Raw XML to the Web: The Need for Presentation

questiontext.text: Why is raw TEI XML unsuitable as a primary reading interface for everyday readers?

generalfeedback.text: Separating semantic data from visual presentation allows digital editions to maintain archival integrity while delivering readable web layouts.

answer.text: Raw XML displays unformatted syntax, angle brackets, and attributes that distract readers from the historical text.

feedback.text: Correct. Separating semantic XML data from HTML/CSS presentation ensures both archival preservation and accessible reading.

answer.text: Web browsers are legally forbidden from opening XML documents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Browsers can open XML, but they display a raw syntax tree that is difficult to read.

answer.text: XML files lose their content unless converted to images.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XML preserves content permanently; presentation simply formats it for human eyes.

answer.text: XML tags can only be read on specialized supercomputers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XML is a lightweight plain-text format readable on any personal computer.

name.text: 02 Question: The Legacy Trap: Monolithic XSLT Stylesheets

questiontext.text: What major problem arose from relying on bespoke XSLT stylesheets in early digital editing projects?

generalfeedback.text: Custom XSLT stylesheets created fragile digital editions that were expensive to maintain and difficult to share across institutions.

answer.text: Bespoke XSLT stylesheets were complex and fragile, creating high maintenance debt when schemas evolved or programmers left.

feedback.text: Correct. Hand-crafted XSLT mixed parsing logic and presentation tags, making stylesheets difficult to maintain or share.

answer.text: XSLT could only produce plain text files without any formatting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XSLT is very powerful and can output HTML and PDF, but complex bespoke code became unmaintainable.

answer.text: XSLT was outlawed by the TEI Consortium in 2005.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XSLT is an open W3C standard, but modern projects prefer declarative processing models.

answer.text: TEI documents could not be parsed by XML transformation engines.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI is valid XML and transforms easily; the issue was procedural stylesheet fragility.

name.text: 03 Question: The TEI Processing Model: Declarative Rendering

questiontext.text: How does the TEI Processing Model simplify the publication of encoded documents?

generalfeedback.text: The TEI Processing Model replaces thousands of lines of procedural code with standardized, declarative rendering instructions.

answer.text: It maps complex TEI tags onto a compact set of standardized, abstract rendering behaviors declared directly in the schema.

feedback.text: Correct. Instead of writing procedural code, editors declare high-level behaviors like paragraph, heading, and note.

answer.text: It replaces XML markup with unformatted Markdown files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The Processing Model operates directly on TEI XML documents.

answer.text: It requires editors to write binary machine code for every element.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The Processing Model is high-level and declarative, not low-level machine code.

answer.text: It restricts digital editions to displaying only five words per page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The model handles complete documents across diverse web and print media.

name.text: 04 Question: The ODD Concept: One Document Does It All

questiontext.text: How does an ODD file function as a 'single source of truth' for a digital editing project?

generalfeedback.text: An ODD file acts as the single source of truth for an edition, generating guidelines, validation schemas, and web stylesheets from one master file.

answer.text: It unites human-readable prose guidelines, formal schema specifications, and visual processing models in one XML master file.

feedback.text: Correct. Compiling an ODD automatically generates Relax NG validation schemas and publication stylesheets from a single source.

answer.text: It forces all project team members to use the exact same computer monitor.

feedback.text: Incorrect. ODD is a document format, not a hardware requirement.

answer.text: It deletes previous editions to prevent other scholars from reading them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. ODD defines project schemas and workflows transparently.

answer.text: It converts all historical languages into modern English automatically.

feedback.text: Incorrect. ODD manages schemas and publication rules, not automated translation.

name.text: 05 Question: The Structure of an ODD File: schemaSpec and elementSpec

questiontext.text: Where are specific element customizations and rendering models declared inside an ODD file?

generalfeedback.text: An ODD file organizes customizations inside elementSpec containers, where each tag receives its description, rules, and rendering models.

answer.text: Inside elementSpec containers nested within the schemaSpec block.

feedback.text: Correct. Each elementSpec names a TEI element and defines its rules, descriptions, and model behaviors.

answer.text: Inside the computer operating system registry files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. All rules are encoded cleanly in standard TEI XML inside the ODD file.

answer.text: In external binary configuration files that cannot be edited in VS Code.

feedback.text: Incorrect. ODD files are plain XML editable in any text editor like VS Code.

answer.text: Inside random comments scattered throughout the project readme.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Customizations are formally structured inside elementSpec elements.

name.text: 06 Question: Core Processing Model Behaviours: Inlines and Blocks

questiontext.text: What is the fundamental difference between inline and block rendering behaviors?

generalfeedback.text: The inline and block behaviours establish the core structure of web layouts, determining whether text flows horizontally or breaks into distinct vertical blocks.

answer.text: Inline elements flow seamlessly within existing text lines, while block elements start on a new line and occupy the full width.

feedback.text: Correct. Inline tags include persName and hi; block tags include div, p, and byline.

answer.text: Inline elements are displayed in red, while block elements are displayed in blue.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Behaviors dictate structural layout, while CSS controls colors.

answer.text: Inline elements can only contain numbers, while blocks can only contain letters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both behaviors can contain any character text.

answer.text: Inline elements are hidden from view, while block elements are visible.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both elements are visible; inline flows horizontally while block creates vertical divisions.

name.text: 07 Question: Document Structure Behaviours: Sections and Breaks

questiontext.text: How do the heading and break behaviors assist in rendering historical documents?

generalfeedback.text: The heading and break behaviours allow editors to represent document divisions and physical manuscript milestones without disrupting reading flow.

answer.text: Heading generates hierarchical section titles, while break formats milestone markers like page breaks and line breaks.

feedback.text: Correct. Milestone tags mark physical manuscript points like pb and lb without enclosing textual content.

answer.text: Heading deletes introductory text, while break stops the web browser from running.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Heading formats titles and break inserts line or page transitions.

answer.text: Heading converts text to uppercase, while break divides words into individual letters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Behaviors handle document structure and milestone transitions.

answer.text: Heading encrypts section names, while break splits documents into separate files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Heading formats h2/h3 headers and break formats physical milestones.

name.text: 08 Question: Critical Editing Behaviours: Notes and Popups

questiontext.text: Why is the note behavior valuable for presenting scholarly commentary in web editions?

generalfeedback.text: The note behaviour separates commentary from the main text flow, presenting critical explanations in sidebars, footnotes, or interactive popups.

answer.text: It decouples annotations from the primary text flow, displaying notes in margins, footnotes, or interactive popups.

feedback.text: Correct. This prevents lengthy commentary notes from cluttering or interrupting the historical text.

answer.text: It erases commentary notes permanently before publishing the website.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The note behavior formats and displays commentary cleanly.

answer.text: It replaces all notes with automated advertisements.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The behavior structures academic commentary for readers.

answer.text: It converts notes into sound effects that play whenever a word is read.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Note behaviors control visual placement in margins, footnotes, or popups.

name.text: 09 Question: Alternate Text Behaviours: Choice and Variations

questiontext.text: How does the alternate behavior support multi-view digital editions?

generalfeedback.text: The alternate behaviour enables multi-view reading, allowing users to inspect diplomatic spellings and normalized readings from a single encoded text.

answer.text: It pairs primary and secondary readings in choice elements, allowing readers to toggle between diplomatic and normalized spellings.

feedback.text: Correct. Readers can view original scribal spelling or modernized text from a single master XML file.

answer.text: It deletes the author's words and substitutes modern poetry.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Alternate presents verified readings like orig/reg or sic/corr.

answer.text: It alternates the text color between red and green on every line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Alternate manages textual variations and editorial choices.

answer.text: It randomly switches words every five seconds to confuse the reader.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Alternate provides controlled, user-selectable views of editorial pairs.

name.text: 10 Question: Tabular and Graphic Behaviours: Tables and Figures

questiontext.text: How do graphic and table behaviors enhance documentary fidelity in digital editions?

generalfeedback.text: The graphic and table behaviours integrate manuscript images, wax seals, and structured accounting ledgers directly alongside transcribed text.

answer.text: They embed high-resolution manuscript facsimiles and format structured accounting ledgers alongside transcribed text.

feedback.text: Correct. Graphic displays images and facsimile surfaces, while table structures financial ledgers and matrices.

answer.text: They replace written sentences with animated video clips.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Graphic and table handle images and tabular data directly.

answer.text: They remove all images to reduce web page loading times to zero.

feedback.text: Incorrect. High-resolution facsimiles provide essential evidence in documentary editing.

answer.text: They force all tables to be displayed as unformatted comma-separated text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Table behaviors produce styled semantic HTML tables.

name.text: 11 Question: Conditional Behaviours: The @predicate Attribute

questiontext.text: How does the predicate attribute enable conditional rendering in the Processing Model?

generalfeedback.text: The predicate attribute uses XPath expressions to apply different rendering behaviors and styles based on element context and attributes.

answer.text: It uses XPath expressions to test conditions, applying specific behaviors and styles based on element attributes or context.

feedback.text: Correct. Predicates allow different styling for philological notes versus historical notes.

answer.text: It automatically corrects grammatical mistakes in student writing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Predicates are conditional tests in XPath, not automated grammar checkers.

answer.text: It deletes any element that contains more than ten characters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Predicates route elements to appropriate rendering rules without deleting data.

answer.text: It forces web browsers to reload the entire operating system.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Predicates simply evaluate XPath conditions during document rendering.

name.text: 12 Question: Multi-Channel Publishing: The @output Attribute

questiontext.text: What is the primary benefit of using the output attribute on model rules?

generalfeedback.text: The output attribute targets rendering rules to specific media, allowing one ODD file to generate both interactive websites and archival print PDFs.

answer.text: It allows editors to target specific media, generating both interactive web editions and print PDFs from one ODD file.

feedback.text: Correct. Rules with output='web' provide clickable popups, while output='print' provides formal page footnotes.

answer.text: It limits publication exclusively to social media platforms.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The output attribute targets standard media formats like web, print, and epub.

answer.text: It requires purchasing a separate software license for every reader.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The Processing Model is open-source and free for all users.

answer.text: It prevents documents from being printed on physical paper.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The print target is specifically optimized for high-quality paper printing.

name.text: 13 Question: Formatting with CSS: Linking ODD to Web Styles

questiontext.text: How does the cssClass attribute connect declarative ODD models to visual styles?

generalfeedback.text: The cssClass attribute binds ODD model rules to external CSS stylesheets, keeping visual styling modular and easy to update.

answer.text: It attaches a class name to generated HTML tags, allowing external CSS stylesheets to control typography, colors, and borders.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps structural rendering rules in the ODD schema while keeping styling modular in external CSS.

answer.text: It embeds raw binary styling code inside the TEI XML header.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CSS is kept in clean external stylesheets.

answer.text: It converts all fonts to comic sans automatically.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Editors choose their own typography in CSS stylesheets.

answer.text: It disables web browsers from using Cascading Style Sheets.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It explicitly enables CSS by assigning classes to rendered elements.

name.text: 14 Question: Modern Web Layouts: CSS Flexbox for Editions

questiontext.text: Why is CSS Flexbox widely used for displaying historical documentary editions?

generalfeedback.text: CSS Flexbox provides an adaptable layout system for presenting manuscript images, transcriptions, and translations in side-by-side reading panes.

answer.text: It aligns manuscript facsimiles, transcriptions, and translations into flexible, equal-height side-by-side reading panes.

feedback.text: Correct. Flexbox provides responsive horizontal alignment that stacks cleanly on smaller screens.

answer.text: It forces all text to bounce up and down across the screen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Flexbox is a modern layout system, not an animation effect.

answer.text: It requires users to write their own browser plugins before reading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Flexbox is built into every modern web browser natively.

answer.text: It only works on computers manufactured before 1995.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Flexbox is a modern W3C standard supported across all contemporary devices.

name.text: 15 Question: Grid Layouts: CSS Grid for Edition Headers and Metadata

questiontext.text: What makes CSS Grid the optimal choice for edition headers and metadata panels?

generalfeedback.text: CSS Grid structures complex archival metadata and edition headers into polished, multi-column card layouts that adapt across screen sizes.

answer.text: It structures complex multi-item information into clean, responsive two-dimensional card layouts with rows and columns.

feedback.text: Correct. Grid excels at organizing archival shelfmarks, dates, repository details, and badges into balanced cards.

answer.text: It replaces all text with mathematical coordinate graphs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CSS Grid arranges HTML layout cards cleanly.

answer.text: It prevents editions from displaying images or hyperlinks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Grid containers can hold any combination of text, images, and links.

answer.text: It limits web pages to a single unformatted vertical column.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Grid specifically enables sophisticated multi-column layouts.

name.text: 16 Question: Styling Inline Entities: People, Places, and Dates

questiontext.text: What is the recommended design practice for styling named entities in a digital edition?

generalfeedback.text: Muted typographic styling and interactive tooltips enrich named entities with Linked Open Data without cluttering the reading experience.

answer.text: Use subtle typographic accents like muted tones or thin dotted underlines, paired with interactive tooltips for Linked Open Data.

feedback.text: Correct. Subtle styling avoids visual noise, preserving comfortable long-form reading while offering rich data on demand.

answer.text: Highlight every entity in bright flashing neon colors across the entire text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Bright neon highlights create visual clutter and distract readers.

answer.text: Hide all named entities completely so nobody can see who was involved.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Entities should be identifiable, but styled with typographic subtlety.

answer.text: Replace historical names with randomly generated modern celebrity names.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scholarly editions maintain absolute fidelity to historical entities.

name.text: 17 Question: Styling Documentary Features: Deletions and Additions

questiontext.text: How should physical manuscript deletions and additions be styled in a documentary web edition?

generalfeedback.text: Clear CSS styling for deletions and additions visualizes physical revisions while allowing readers to inspect scribal corrections effortlessly.

answer.text: Render deletions with strikethrough lines and muted color, and additions with superscript positioning or distinct tints.

feedback.text: Correct. This clearly communicates scribal revisions to scholars while maintaining readability.

answer.text: Erase deleted words silently from the edition so readers never know they existed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Documentary editing preserves cancellations as vital evidence of authorial intent.

answer.text: Display deleted words in giant red letters that cover the rest of the page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Muted strikethrough lines signal cancellation without obscuring surrounding text.

answer.text: Convert all scribal additions into separate downloadable sound files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Additions are visual text features formatted with superscript or carets.

name.text: 18 Question: Cohort Presentation: Ace's French Revolutionary Decree

questiontext.text: What presentation features are most important for Ace's 1791 French Revolutionary decree edition?

generalfeedback.text: Ace's French decree requires formal legislative typography, numbered article cards, and a dual-column display comparing diplomatic and modernized text.

answer.text: Formal legislative typography, numbered decree articles, and a dual-column layout comparing diplomatic text with modernized French.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the official nature of the Imprimerie Royale print and facilitates historical linguistic comparison.

answer.text: Bright comic book illustrations and informal handwritten fonts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The decree is an official legal artifact requiring formal legislative typography.

answer.text: Hiding the French text and only showing modern English summaries.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scholarly editions showcase the primary historical language alongside translations.

answer.text: Deleting the royal title banner to pretend the king was never involved.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The decree reflects the 1791 constitutional monarchy, requiring authentic historical paratexts.

name.text: 19 Question: Cohort Presentation: Olyvia's Maud Lewis Letter

questiontext.text: Which design strategy best reflects the epistolary nature of Olyvia's 1967 Maud Lewis letter?

generalfeedback.text: Olyvia's Maud Lewis edition emphasizes the intimate epistolary artifact, pairing handwritten lineation and physical stationery with folk art popups.

answer.text: Preserving handwritten lineation, displaying postal stationery headers, and embedding popups for referenced folk art paintings.

feedback.text: Correct. This honors the intimate physical artifact while connecting Maud's words to her artwork.

answer.text: Formatting the personal letter as a formal international peace treaty.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The document is an intimate handwritten letter requiring epistolary presentation.

answer.text: Erasing all line breaks to force the letter into a single giant paragraph.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Preserving line breaks captures the natural rhythm of Maud's handwritten sentences.

answer.text: Replacing Maud's handwriting scans with stock photos of modern cities.

feedback.text: Incorrect. High-resolution facsimiles of the actual stationery provide crucial material context.

name.text: 20 Question: Cohort Presentation: Andromeda's 1752 Peace and Friendship Treaty

questiontext.text: How should Andromeda's web edition represent the diplomatic signatures and clauses of the 1752 treaty?

generalfeedback.text: Andromeda's treaty edition requires dignified legal typography, visual representations of totem marks and seals, and interactive commentary popups.

answer.text: With spacious legal clauses, numbered Roman numerals, inline graphics of Mi'kmaw totem marks and wax seals, and legal popups.

feedback.text: Correct. This respects the diplomatic solemnity of the agreement and highlights Indigenous and colonial signatories.

answer.text: By removing all references to Mi'kmaw delegates and presenting the treaty as a private business contract.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The treaty is a nation-to-nation peace agreement signed by Mi'kmaw leaders with totem marks.

answer.text: By converting the treaty clauses into rhyming stanzas of poetry.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The edition must maintain legal fidelity and formal clause structure.

answer.text: By omitting the wax seals because they take up too much screen space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scanned seals and totem marks authenticate the legal authority of the historical witness.

name.text: 21 Question: Building Interactive Toggles with HTML and CSS

questiontext.text: What is the pedagogical purpose of providing interactive view toggles in a digital edition?

generalfeedback.text: Interactive toggles give readers control over their reading experience, allowing them to switch between diplomatic and normalized views effortlessly.

answer.text: They empower diverse users to switch between diplomatic, normalized, and commentary views on demand without reloading.

feedback.text: Correct. Toggles accommodate different research needs, from paleographical analysis to smooth long-form reading.

answer.text: They prevent unauthorized visitors from reading the primary source.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Toggles enrich access by offering multiple verified views of the text.

answer.text: They force readers to restart their web browser whenever they change views.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Modern toggles update layout instantly without page reloads.

answer.text: They randomly delete sentences to test if the reader is paying attention.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Toggles switch between structured editorial layers transparently.

name.text: 22 Question: Typography for Historical Texts: Hierarchy and Readability

questiontext.text: Why are serif typefaces with generous line spacing recommended for historical text editions?

generalfeedback.text: Thoughtful typography with serif typefaces, generous line height, and balanced contrast ensures sustained reading comfort for historical editions.

answer.text: Serif letterforms guide the eye smoothly across long lines, while generous spacing prevents eye fatigue during sustained reading.

feedback.text: Correct. Combining quality serifs with 1.6 line height and balanced contrast ensures comfortable reading.

answer.text: Serif fonts load one hundred times faster than sans-serif fonts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Font loading speed depends on file size, not letterform design.

answer.text: Serif typefaces are required by federal copyright legislation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Typography choices are based on legibility, aesthetics, and user comfort.

answer.text: Line spacing should be zero so all text forms a solid block of ink.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Zero line spacing causes overlapping text that is completely unreadable.

name.text: 23 Question: Responsive Design: Supporting Mobile and Desktop

questiontext.text: How does responsive web design accommodate users accessing editions on smartphones?

generalfeedback.text: Responsive design uses CSS media queries to stack side-by-side reading panes vertically on mobile screens, ensuring universal accessibility.

answer.text: It uses CSS media queries to stack side-by-side reading panes vertically, eliminating horizontal scrolling on small screens.

feedback.text: Correct. Responsive layouts adapt fluidly, ensuring mobile readers can view facsimiles and text comfortably.

answer.text: It blocks mobile phones from accessing the website entirely.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Responsive design ensures mobile devices are fully supported.

answer.text: It deletes all images and commentary when viewed on a phone.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Responsive design reorganizes layouts without stripping essential scholarly content.

answer.text: It forces smartphone users to download a paid mobile application.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Responsive web pages run natively in any standard mobile browser.

name.text: 24 Question: Accessibility (a11y) in Digital Textual Editions

questiontext.text: What three core practices ensure a digital edition meets high web accessibility standards?

generalfeedback.text: Accessible editions use semantic HTML landmarks, descriptive alt text, and full keyboard navigation to ensure all scholars can explore historical documents.

answer.text: Using semantic HTML landmarks, providing descriptive alt text for images, and enabling full keyboard navigation.

feedback.text: Correct. These practices ensure screen reader users and keyboard-only users can navigate the edition independently.

answer.text: Using unformatted plain text, disabling all images, and removing links.

feedback.text: Incorrect. True accessibility enriches rich media with semantic tags and alternatives.

answer.text: Requiring biometric fingerprint scans before viewing historical documents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Accessibility removes barriers to access rather than creating new ones.

answer.text: Writing the entire edition in encrypted computer code.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Editions must be clear, transparent, and navigable for all users.

name.text: 25 Question: Web Components and TEI Publisher

questiontext.text: What advantage do Web Components provide when building digital publishing platforms?

generalfeedback.text: Web Components package complex interactive features like deep-zoom image viewers and ODD renderers into reusable custom HTML tags.

answer.text: They package complex behaviors like deep-zoom image viewers and ODD rendering into reusable custom HTML tags.

feedback.text: Correct. Components like pb-facsimile and pb-view make building digital editions modular and robust.

answer.text: They replace web browsers with physical printed books.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Web components are modern browser technologies.

answer.text: They automatically delete the project repository after thirty days.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Web components are durable, reusable interface building blocks.

answer.text: They require users to manually type out binary code to view an image.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Web components handle complex pan-and-zoom functionality behind simple tags.

name.text: 26 Question: Static Site Generation: Minimal Computing for Editions

questiontext.text: Why is static site generation considered a cornerstone of sustainable digital humanities?

generalfeedback.text: Static site generation embodies minimal computing, producing durable HTML files that survive for decades without server maintenance or database costs.

answer.text: Pre-compiled static HTML and CSS files endure for decades without requiring active server databases or security maintenance.

feedback.text: Correct. Minimal computing eliminates database vulnerabilities and ongoing server costs, ensuring long-term survival.

answer.text: Static sites can only display black-and-white text without graphics.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Static websites can include high-resolution images, rich styling, and interactive features.

answer.text: Static sites automatically erase themselves after five years.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Plain HTML and CSS files survive indefinitely because they have zero software dependencies.

answer.text: Static sites require paying expensive monthly fees to cloud database companies.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Static sites can be hosted completely free on platforms like GitHub Pages.

name.text: 27 Question: Previewing Your Edition Locally in VS Code

questiontext.text: How do VS Code Live Server and browser DevTools accelerate edition development?

generalfeedback.text: Using VS Code Live Server and browser developer tools enables rapid local testing and fine-tuning of your digital edition layouts.

answer.text: Live Server provides instant browser reloads upon saving, while DevTools allow real-time inspection of HTML and CSS rules.

feedback.text: Correct. This rapid local feedback loop lets editors refine typography, margins, and layouts efficiently.

answer.text: They automatically translate 18th-century French into modern German.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Live Server and DevTools are web development and inspection tools.

answer.text: They upload your files to public search engines without your permission.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Live Server runs strictly on your local machine (127.0.0.1).

answer.text: They convert your computer into a physical printing press.

feedback.text: Incorrect. They provide an interactive digital preview inside your local web browser.

name.text: 28 Question: Quality Gate: Validating HTML and CSS Outputs

questiontext.text: What key areas must be audited before publishing your digital edition to the web?

generalfeedback.text: A pre-publication quality audit verifies HTML validity, image asset paths, commentary pointers, and mobile responsiveness across your entire edition.

answer.text: HTML syntax validity, external stylesheet linkage, image asset paths, commentary pointer resolution, and mobile responsiveness.

feedback.text: Correct. Systematically verifying these areas eliminates broken links, 404 errors, and layout glitches.

answer.text: Whether the website matches the color of the author's modern automobile.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Quality audits verify technical markup, asset resolution, and responsiveness.

answer.text: Checking that all files have been converted into proprietary Word documents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Digital editions are delivered in open web formats like HTML and CSS.

answer.text: Verifying that no human beings have read the text prior to publication.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Peer review and human verification are essential quality standards.

name.text: 29 Question: Today's Studio Lab: Designing Your Edition Styles

questiontext.text: What are the three core milestones of today's classroom studio lab in Mulroney Hall 3032?

generalfeedback.text: Today's lab guides you to define typographic rules, implement document-specific layouts, and verify your presentation locally in VS Code.

answer.text: Define base typographic style rules, implement document-specific feature layouts, and verify rendering locally in Live Server.

feedback.text: Correct. Students craft stylesheets for their witness, build layouts, and test interactive popups locally.

answer.text: Write a twenty-page paper on ancient Greek pottery.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Today's lab focuses on digital edition styling and web presentation.

answer.text: Delete the XML files created earlier in the semester.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The lab builds directly upon the semester's master TEI XML files.

answer.text: Reinstall the computer operating system from scratch.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Students work directly in VS Code with their existing workspace files.

questiontext.text: When and where will our final class meeting take place, and what is its capstone focus?

generalfeedback.text: Today you styled your digital edition with modern web layouts; on Friday at 10:30 AM, we conclude our capstone studio with multi-modal archiving and public release.

feedback.text: Correct. Thursday is Patronal Feast Day; Friday runs on a Wednesday timetable to complete our capstone publication studio.

answer.text: Saturday at midnight in the campus library basement, focusing on video games.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Meeting 36 takes place Friday at 10:30 AM in MULH 3032.

answer.text: Classes are permanently cancelled and no final deliverables are required.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Friday concludes the studio and prepares the final portfolio deposit.

answer.text: Friday at 8:30 AM in the university gymnasium.

feedback.text: Incorrect. StFX runs a Wednesday timetable on Friday Dec 4, meeting at 10:30 AM in Mulroney 3032.
